name: Anthropic Claude
desc: Frontier models strong at long context, code and careful reasoning. Use for agents and analysis over large documents.

name: OpenAI
desc: GPT models with the widest tooling and ecosystem support. Use when you want the most examples to copy from.

name: Google Gemini
desc: Multimodal models with very large context and native Google Cloud integration. Use for video, audio and GCP-resident data.

name: Mistral AI
desc: European models with strong open-weight releases. Use when data residency in the EU is a requirement.

name: Groq
desc: Open models served at extreme token speed on custom LPU hardware. Use when latency is the product. Not the same company as xAI's Grok.

name: AWS Bedrock
desc: Many vendors' models behind one AWS-governed API. Use when procurement and IAM must own model access.

name: Grok (xAI)
desc: xAI frontier models with live access to X. Use when real-time public conversation matters to the answer.

name: Ollama
desc: Run open models locally with one command. Use for offline development and privacy-sensitive prototypes.

name: vLLM
desc: High-throughput inference server with paged attention. Use when you self-host a model for real production traffic.

name: Hugging Face
desc: Model and dataset hub with the transformers library. Use to find, fine-tune and host open models.

name: llama.cpp
desc: Quantised model inference on ordinary CPUs and laptops. Use to embed a small model in a desktop app.

name: LangChain
desc: Chains, tools and agent scaffolding across providers. Use when swapping models and stitching steps is the main job.

name: LlamaIndex
desc: Ingestion, indexing and retrieval pipelines for documents. Use when RAG over your own corpus is the whole product.

name: Vercel AI SDK
desc: Streaming, tool calls and structured output with one TypeScript API. Use in Next.js and React chat interfaces.

name: Pydantic AI
desc: Typed agents with validated structured output. Use when the model result must fit a schema you can trust.

name: Model Context Protocol
desc: Open standard for exposing tools and data to any AI client. Use to write one integration instead of one per assistant.

name: Claude Code
desc: Terminal agent that reads, edits and runs your repository. Use for multi-file refactors and long autonomous tasks.

name: Cursor
desc: AI-first editor forked from VS Code. Use when you want inline completion and chat in one familiar IDE.

name: GitHub Copilot
desc: Inline completion and chat inside existing IDEs. Use when enterprise licensing already covers it.

name: Aider
desc: Terminal pair programmer that commits to git as it works. Use when you want every AI change as a reviewable commit.

name: NotebookLM
desc: Grounded research notebook over documents you upload, with citations. Use to interrogate a pile of PDFs without building a pipeline.

name: Firecrawl
desc: Turns websites into clean markdown for model consumption. Use when your knowledge base is other people's web pages.

name: Unstructured
desc: Parses PDFs, slides and scans into structured chunks. Use when the source documents are a mess.

name: Langfuse
desc: Open-source tracing, cost tracking and evals for LLM apps. Use to find out which prompt is burning your budget.

name: LangSmith
desc: Hosted tracing and evaluation from the LangChain team. Use when already deep in LangChain.

name: Braintrust
desc: Eval-driven development with datasets and scoring in CI. Use to stop prompt changes silently regressing quality.

name: Weights & Biases
desc: Experiment tracking, sweeps and model registry. Use when you actually train models rather than only call them.
